findings.title: Migration crashes when the legacy embed_category setting was never persisted
findings.body: The migration dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] for a query joining site_settings to categories on the embed_category setting. Site settings that were never customized are not stored as rows, so for the common case where embed_category was never set this query returns zero rows, [0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and the deploy/upgrade. The fallback on lines 14-16 makes the same assumption about an uncategorized_category_id row existing. The migration must handle missing rows (e.g. check cmd_tuples / nil before indexing) and fall back safely.

findings.title: Migration inserts legacy hosts verbatim, bypassing normalization, so migrated hosts stop matching
findings.body: Legacy embeddable_hosts values are inserted with raw SQL instead of going through EmbeddableHost, so the model's before_validation stripping of scheme and path never runs. Values previously accepted and handled by SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? such as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' are stored verbatim, while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) against URI(referer).host (e.g. 'discourse.org'), so those migrated hosts will never be allowed after the upgrade and embedding silently breaks for them. The unescaped interpolation of h into the INSERT also breaks the migration if a stored value contains a single quote. Normalize (and safely quote/bind) each host before inserting it.

findings.title: Host format validation is inconsistent with host lookup and rejects valid hosts
findings.body: The format regex allows an optional port (:[0-9]{1,5}), but record_for_host looks up URI(host).host, which strips the port, so a saved host like 'example.com:8080' can never equal the stored string and will never be allowed or assigned a category. Conversely the regex restricts the TLD to 2-5 letters, rejecting valid embed hosts the old free-form setting accepted, such as example.museum or example.technology. Validation, storage normalization, and lookup need to agree on ports and TLD length.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on a nil host instead of failing validation
findings.body: The before_validation block calls self.host.sub! unconditionally. When host is nil (EmbeddableHost.new with no attributes, or a create/update request missing the host param), this raises NoMethodError and produces a 500 rather than a validation error rendered by render_json_error. There is also no presence validation for host or category_id. Guard the normalization for blank values and add a presence validation so invalid input is reported cleanly.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint on host makes the host-to-category mapping ambiguous
findings.body: Nothing prevents duplicate host rows: the model has no uniqueness validation and the migration creates the table without a unique index. An admin can create the same host twice with different categories, after which record_for_host's unordered .first picks an arbitrary row, so topics imported from that host are filed into a nondeterministic category and host_allowed?/category behavior depends on database row order. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique database index (after normalizing case in storage).

findings.title: Update and destroy raise NoMethodError for a nonexistent host id
findings.body: Both update (line 10) and destroy (line 15) use EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then immediately call save_host(host) or host.destroy. For a stale or invalid id the record is nil, so save_host fails setting host.host and destroy fails on nil.destroy, returning a 500 instead of a 404. Look the record up with find (letting ActiveRecord raise RecordNotFound) or explicitly render a not-found error when it is absent.

findings.title: Clicking edit crashes when the host has no resolved category
findings.body: The edit action does this.get('host.category.id') without checking that category exists. A host's category is undefined when its category was deleted, and also right after saving a new host without choosing a category: save() sets category from Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')) with a null categoryId while the server silently defaults to the uncategorized category, leaving host.category undefined in the client. Clicking the pencil then throws a TypeError and the row can no longer be edited until a page reload. Guard the lookup (host.category && host.category.id) and set the client category to what the server actually assigned.

findings.title: Category and embeddable-host fabricator file contents are swapped
findings.body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now contains only the embeddable_host fabricator, while the newly added spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all of the category fabricators (category, diff_category, happy_category, private_category). Tests still pass because Fabrication loads every file regardless of name, but the mislabeled files are misleading and invite duplicate-definition mistakes when someone edits the file matching the fabricator name. Move each definition into the file named after it.

findings.title: New admin endpoints have no behavioral test coverage
findings.body: The specs for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController only assert that the classes inherit from Admin::AdminController. None of the new behavior is exercised: create/update success and validation failure, the blank-category fallback to the uncategorized category in save_host, destroy, or the embedding show payload with its hosts. Regressions in these endpoints (including the nil-record handling) would not be caught. Add request/controller specs covering those paths for a logged-in admin.
